images.caption: New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina: A section of Jackson Barracks, a military base in New Orleans established after the War of 1812. National Guard troops and relief supplies were stationed here for Hurricane Katrina. As this section of the city, in the Lower 9th Ward, was one of the first to flood catastrophically, troops had their hands full saving themselves in the disaster. Some succeeded in launching boats and helping save people in the neighborhood, but much equipment and supplies were lost.

images.caption:
New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina: Sign at an entrance to Jackson Barracks, a military base in New Orleans established after the War of 1812. National Guard troops and relief supplies were stationed here for Hurricane Katrina. As this section of the city, in the Lower 9th Ward, was one of the first to flood catastrophically, troops had their hands full saving themselves in the disaster. Some succeeded in launching boats and helping save people in the neighborhood, but much equipment and supplies were lost.
Note lines  of various levels of long standing water can be seen. Highest water was a rapidly rising storm surge which necessitated people effect to either run upstairs in multi story buildings where that was an option or swim for their lives.

images.caption:
General view across the aircraft exhibits of the Louisiana Military museum. The museum was still trying to recover from the damage caused by Hurricane Katrina in 2005, during which the entire area was under deep water.
Visible from left to right are:-
F-86D Sabre '23747' really 52-4168,
F-4C Phantom II '63-556' (63-7556),
F-15A Eagle 73-0086,
F-102A Delta Dagger '62334' really YF-102A 53-1787
and
A-26C Invader '435937' (44-35937).
Jackson Barracks, New Orleans.
Louisiana, USA.
